report.tagline: A short video app that shows you an endless feed picked by what you watch, not who you follow.
report.simpleSummary: TikTok is an app full of short videos, usually 15 seconds to a few minutes long. You open it and a video starts playing right away. You swipe up for the next one. It learns what you like from how long you watch each video, so in a few minutes the feed feels made for you. It makes money from ads and from TikTok Shop, where you can buy things you see in videos.

overview.whatItDoes: TikTok shows a full-screen feed of short videos called the For You page. Anyone can film, edit and post a video with music and effects inside the app. A strong recommendation system decides who sees each video. TikTok has been banned in India since June 2020, so Indian users moved to Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Moj and Josh.
howItWorks: The app opens straight into a video. No need to follow anyone first.
It watches signals like watch time, replays, likes, shares and skips to guess what you like.
Every new video is shown to a small group first. If they watch it fully, it is shown to a bigger group. So an unknown creator can go viral.
Creators use built-in tools: music library, filters, duets, stitches and the CapCut editor.
Brands pay for ads in the feed, and sellers list products in TikTok Shop that creators sell through videos and live streams.
overview.valueProposition: Instant entertainment that feels personal, with no work to set up. For creators, a real chance to go viral without existing followers.

painPoints.pain: Finding fun content takes effort on apps where you must follow people first.
painPoints.howSolved: The For You feed works from the first second, using an interest graph instead of a friend list.

painPoints.pain: New creators get no reach on follower-based apps.
painPoints.howSolved: Every video gets a test audience, so quality can win over follower count.

painPoints.pain: Making a good video needs editing skills.
painPoints.howSolved: Built-in music, effects and templates, plus CapCut, make editing easy.

painPoints.pain: Brands find it hard to reach young people who skip TV and banner ads.
painPoints.howSolved: Native-looking ads and creator partnerships inside the feed.

painPoints.pain: Shopping online feels boring and hard to trust.
painPoints.howSolved: TikTok Shop lets people buy from a video or live stream where they see the product in use.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: An endless, personal feed of videos chosen by the recommendation system.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: It is the product. It keeps people watching and creates ad slots.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Camera, sounds library, filters, duets, stitches and templates.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Makes posting easy, so there is always fresh content to feed the algorithm.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Any audio can be reused by others, which starts trends and challenges.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Trends spread fast and pull users in, and TikTok became a top place to discover music.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shoppable videos, live shopping and an in-app store with affiliate commissions for creators.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The fastest-growing revenue source, turning watching into buying.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Live streams where viewers buy coins and send virtual gifts to creators.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Direct money from fans, with TikTok keeping a large share.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Search videos by topic, used by many young people like a search engine.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Opens a new ad format and competes with Google for young users.

steps.detail: Video plays at once, even before signing up.
Taps a few topics like comedy or pets.
Watches some videos fully, skips others. The app learns fast.
Within 20 to 30 minutes, the feed shows mostly what they like.
Creates an account to like, follow and comment.
Returns several times a day, averaging close to 1 hour a day.
Shoots 30 seconds on the phone camera.
Picks audio from the trending list.
Video shown to a few hundred people first.
Watch-through rate is high, so TikTok pushes it to thousands, then millions.
Joins Creator Rewards and gets brand and Shop affiliate offers.
Uploads a serum with price and stock.
Video shows before-and-after results with an orange cart link.
Seller ships or uses Fulfilled by TikTok.
Seller runs live streams with discounts to drive more sales.

businessModel.summary: TikTok makes most of its money from ads shown between videos. It also earns a commission on TikTok Shop sales and a cut of virtual gifts on LIVE.

revenueStreams.detail: In-feed ads, TopView ads that play when the app opens, branded hashtag challenges and search ads.
TikTok takes a referral fee on each sale, often around 6% to 8% in the US (estimate), plus fees for fulfilment and promotions.
Users buy coins and send gifts to creators. TikTok keeps a large share, reported at around half.
Creator subscriptions and paid business tools bring in smaller amounts.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. Ads bought through TikTok Ads Manager, often with a minimum daily budget of about $50 per campaign. Shop fees vary by country.
costDrivers: Video storage and streaming bandwidth for billions of daily views
Content moderation teams and AI to remove harmful videos
Creator payouts through Creator Rewards and LIVE gifts
Discounts and free shipping subsidies to grow TikTok Shop
Compliance costs like Project Texas, Project Clover in Europe and the US joint venture
businessModel.unitEconomics: A US user watching about 55 minutes a day sees dozens of ads. If TikTok earns roughly $40 to $60 a year from that user in ads (estimate), and spends a few dollars a year on streaming and moderation, the user is very profitable. Users in poorer markets bring in a dollar or two a year, so they help mostly with content and scale. In Shop, on a $30 order, TikTok might keep $2 to $3 in fees but often spends some of that on discounts to grow.

howTheyGetUsers: Videos shared to WhatsApp, Instagram and other apps with the TikTok watermark
Heavy paid marketing in its early years
Trends and sounds that spill into culture, news and music charts
No sign-up needed to start watching
whatBringsUsersBack: Variable reward: the next video might be great, so people keep swiping
Notifications about new videos from creators they follow
Creators returning to check views and comments
growth.moat: The recommendation system is trained on billions of daily watch signals. The more people watch, the better it gets at guessing what each person wants. Creators also go where viewers are, which makes it hard for a new app to catch up.

competitors.name: Instagram Reels
competitors.positioning: Short video inside Instagram, built on your follow graph. The biggest short video app in India since TikTok's ban.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: TikTok is fully interest-led and was built for video first. Reels mixes in friends and Instagram's huge existing user base.

competitors.name: YouTube Shorts
competitors.positioning: Short videos inside YouTube, linking to long videos.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: YouTube has better revenue sharing and long-form content. TikTok's feed is stronger at fast discovery.

competitors.name: Moj and Josh (India)
competitors.positioning: Indian short video apps that grew after TikTok was banned in 2020, focused on regional languages.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: They copied the TikTok format but struggled to make money and keep users once Reels and Shorts arrived.

competitors.name: Douyin
competitors.positioning: ByteDance's sister app in China, with deep shopping and local services.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Douyin shows where TikTok wants to go: a shopping and payments app as much as an entertainment app.

northStar.metric: Daily time spent watching videos users enjoy (watch time from fully watched or liked videos)
northStar.why: TikTok's value is entertainment that fits you. Time spent on videos people finish or like shows real enjoyment, not just mindless scrolling. More good watch time also means more ad slots and Shop sales.

Huge creator base and culture-shaping trends

improvementIdeas.idea: Feed control panel with topic sliders
improvementIdeas.problem: Users feel the feed gets stuck on one topic or too much shopping.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Users feel in control, which can raise satisfaction and long-term retention.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: 'Not interested' taps per user and 30-day retention

improvementIdeas.idea: Shop trust badge based on return rates and verified reviews
improvementIdeas.problem: Buyers fear fake or poor products.

improvementIdeas.idea: Clear reasons and quick appeals for removed videos
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Less creator churn and fewer support tickets.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Creator 90-day retention and appeal resolution time

improvementIdeas.idea: Mindful mode with daily summary and soft stop
improvementIdeas.problem: Users and regulators worry about addiction.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better trust with parents and regulators, small hit on time spent.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of teens using the mode, and daily active users over 90 days

pmLessons: An interest graph can beat a social graph. TikTok won by showing good content to anyone, not just content from friends.
Remove the cold start. TikTok works in the first minute without follows or setup.
Give supply a fair chance. Letting unknown creators go viral kept fresh videos coming.
Policy is product risk. TikTok lost India overnight in 2020, showing that a great product can still be stopped by government.

interviewQuestions.question: TikTok is banned in India. If you were PM of Instagram Reels, how would you win the users TikTok left behind?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment ex-TikTok users (small-town creators, regional languages). Talk about creator tools, regional content, monetisation, and a metric like daily creators from tier 2 and 3 cities.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between an interest graph and a social graph? Which is better for a new app?
interviewQuestions.hint: Interest graph uses behaviour, social graph uses friends. Interest graph solves the empty feed problem early but is harder to build.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the health of the For You feed?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick watch time on enjoyed videos as the main metric, then watch-through rate, skips, 'not interested' taps, and guardrails like harmful content reports.

interviewQuestions.question: Should TikTok push more Shop videos in the feed?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh Shop revenue against user annoyance. Propose a test, track purchase rate and also session length and retention.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did Moj and Josh struggle after TikTok's ban?
interviewQuestions.hint: Talk about weaker recommendations, paying creators to post, no ad business at scale, and Reels and Shorts arriving with huge built-in audiences.
